entry.title: Buying with a mortgage in NYC comes with an extra tax
entry.summary: House and condo buyers who borrow face a recording tax that a comparable cash purchase avoids. What does that add, and is the distinction fair?

entry.title: At $2 million, one extra dollar adds about $5,000 in tax
entry.summary: New York City sales shifted below $2 million after a new tax step arrived in 2019. The records show how a line in the tax code changed the prices people recorded.

entry.title: The cash discount shrinks after screening possible family transfers
entry.summary: A comparison of repeat house sales finds a sizeable cash-mortgage gap. Removing possible transfers between relatives roughly halves it.

entry.title: A foreclosure deed’s dollar amount may not be a sale price
entry.summary: When lenders take title, legal rules can shape the amount in the record. Including those transfers changes a constructed house-price index through the financial crisis.

entry.title: The condo data gap is much wider in the Bronx
entry.summary: The same public-record match links about four in five eligible Manhattan sales to a deed, but fewer than half in the Bronx. That changes which transactions appear in financing comparisons.
